name: Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS IS 10500:2012)
description: Indian Standard Drinking Water Specification (Second Revision). Outlines acceptable limits and permissible limits in the absence of an alternate source.
source: Bureau of Indian Standards, IS 10500 : 2012 Drinking Water Specification

turbidity.notes: Desirable 1.0 NTU; permissible up to 5.0 NTU in absence of alternate source.

tds.notes: Desirable 500 mg/L; permissible up to 2000 mg/L.

hardness.notes: Desirable 200 mg/L; permissible up to 600 mg/L.

chloride.notes: Desirable 250 mg/L; permissible up to 1000 mg/L.

dissolved_oxygen.notes: Operational parameter; dissolved oxygen >= 4 mg/L prevents septic conditions.

lead.notes: 0.01 mg/L maximum; toxic metal, no relaxation.

arsenic.notes: Desirable 0.01 mg/L; permissible 0.05 mg/L in absence of alternate source.

iron.notes: 1.0 mg/L maximum permissible limit; causes staining.

name: World Health Organization Guidelines (WHO 2022)
description: Guidelines for Drinking-water Quality, 4th edition incorporating the 1st and 2nd addenda. Global international benchmarks.
source: WHO Guidelines for Drinking-water Quality, 4th Edition

ph.notes: Operational guideline 6.5-8.5 to prevent corrosion and maintain chlorination efficacy.

turbidity.notes: Guideline: ideally < 0.2 NTU for disinfection; median < 1 NTU in distribution.

tds.notes: Palatability threshold: <600 mg/L good, >1000 mg/L increasingly unacceptable.

hardness.notes: Aesthetic guideline; scale occurs above 200 mg/L CaCO3.

nitrate.notes: 50 mg/L as NO3 to protect bottle-fed infants against methemoglobinemia.

chloride.notes: Taste threshold 250 mg/L; corrosion acceleration above this level.

dissolved_oxygen.notes: Operational indicator of water freshness; >= 5.0 mg/L recommended.

arsenic.notes: Provisional health-based guideline value 0.01 mg/L (10 ug/L).

name: US EPA National Drinking Water Standards
description: United States Environmental Protection Agency National Primary (health) and Secondary (aesthetic) Regulations.
source: EPA 816-F-09-004 National Primary Drinking Water Regulations

turbidity.notes: Primary MCL: <= 0.3 NTU in 95% of monthly samples, never exceed 1.0 NTU.

hardness.notes: Guideline: 0-60 soft, 61-120 moderate, 121-180 hard, >180 very hard.

nitrate.notes: MCL is 10 mg/L as Nitrogen (N), which equals ~44.3 - 45 mg/L as Nitrate (NO3-).

iron.notes: SMCL: 0.3 mg/L for color, taste, staining.
